metric: planBefore/planAfter pairs from Calcite's current rule tests, translated to SQL, proved equivalent; 1 genuine Calcite non-equivalence refuted with a DuckDB counterexample, 136 unknown. 83 of the 168 pairs new to every other corpus are proved.
caveats: Calcite commit 2d28ce3 (2026-09-30). 502 of 1016 tests translate exactly; 182 leave the plan unchanged (not rewrites) and 332 are skipped with reasons (tests/fixtures/calcite_mined/skipped.jsonl). 334 of the 502 overlap SQLSolver, QED or R-Bot, whose pairs rules were developed against (tuned on test); the 168 new pairs were not used for development. While building the ANY/ALL rules, 7 held-out pairs were read (testJoinConditionOrExpansionRuleAnti, testNullSelect2, testSomeWithGreaterThanNoRowSubQuery, testSomeWithLessThanOrEqualNoRowSubQuery, testTopDownGeneralDecorrelateForFilterSome, testTopDownGeneralDecorrelateForSubqueryWithJoin, testNotInNullableKey); 2 of them are proved, so 61 of the 63 held-out proofs are clean. Three more held-out pairs (testCorrelatedFilterWithVariable, testFilterIntoJoinMissingVariableCor, testTopDownGeneralDecorrelateForLateralJoin) were seen through the failing-tests triage while building the decorrelation rules.
correctness: 0 false proofs; every proof and refutation re-run on 60 random DuckDB databases, half skewed towards the literals
held_out: 83/168 on pairs new to every other corpus, tuned on test: they scored 53/168 before any rule was developed against them; the set-operation rules were written with their unknowns in view, and 7 were read while building the ANY/ALL rules (quantified_rules.py). The decorrelation rules (decorrelation_rules.py) lifted them from 78 to 83, all 5 seen during development: 3 through the failing-tests triage and 2 of the 7 read for the ANY/ALL rules, so they add no clean held-out evidence.
